PARTIALLY LANDED at a9f20a5 by the chief. The CONTRACT half is done; the false-declaration half is NOT, and the bead stays open for it.

DONE: SourceView now STATES the node-totality invariant, and SourceViewLaws asserts it over both implementations from generated data, plus the consequence that every exposed ref has a measured discourse span. Shipped with a foil -- a view whose adjacency names a ref outside its node index -- because both real implementations pass and a law with no capacity to fail is not evidence.

Verified by MUTATION, not by counting: munit prints no individual test names here, so 86 passing proves nothing about whether my four new properties registered. Flipping the foil's assertion failed that named test with 85 siblings passing. Making positionsAreMeasured return false failed both checkAll properties BY NAME on InMemorySourceView and StorySourceView -- which also rules out vacuity, since those properties run through .validated.forall and would pass trivially if validation returned None.

Gate: lawsJVM 86, lawsJS 86, alignJVM 192, GATE_EXIT=0, format clean, tests re-run after scalafmtAll changed the files.

STILL OPEN, and this is the original bead: signature.scala:392 and population.scala:271 declare SourceNodeRef => Option[Double] and implement it as Some(view.relativePosition(r)) -- an Option that structurally cannot be None, one line above a worldPos that uses the same channel correctly. The law makes the underlying value trustworthy; it does NOT fix the type that lies about it. That remains a false declaration whether or not a caller trips it.

Whoever takes the remainder: the law now guarantees relativePosition is meaningful for every exposed ref, so the honest fix is probably to DROP the Option from discoursePos rather than to thread None through it -- the absence channel is unnecessary now that the invariant is enforced, and an unnecessary Option is how this started. Do not assume that without checking worldPos, which genuinely needs its Option.

Reservations released; I hold nothing on this bead.
